sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Elizabeth, NJ different from other Union County towns?
sections.html:
Elizabeth is a dense port city: 141,675 residents on 12.32 square miles of land, about 11,145 people per square mile by the 2020 count. Only 25.6 percent of homes are owner occupied, so many houses for sale are two, three and four family buildings that investors and live-in owners both compete for. Median value of owner-occupied homes is $449,300 for 2020 to 2024, and median household income is $66,555.

That mix shapes what buyers ask about. Median gross rent is $1,523, and the household count is 46,121 at 2.95 people each.

sections.h2: Where is Elizabeth, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
The city sits in Union County between Newark to the north and Linden to the southwest, with Roselle, Roselle Park, Union and Hillside to the west. Newark Bay and the Arthur Kill form its eastern edge, and the Goethals Bridge lands here on the way to Staten Island. The Elizabeth River runs 4.2 miles through the city, mostly in a channel.

The street plan is unusual for New Jersey. Instead of a grid, it is largely circular, with streets radiating from the central railroad station. A buyer driving the neighborhoods will notice that a house a block from Elizabeth station and one near Warinanco Park are very different propositions.

sections.h2: Which Elizabeth neighborhoods do buyers talk about?
sections.html:

Because housing type changes block by block, a good listing names the neighborhood and the number of units in the first line.

sections.h2: What does the city require before an Elizabeth house can be sold?
sections.html:
Elizabeth has an online Resale Certificates application, and the form asks you to attach the smoke detector certificate if the property is occupied. Ask the City of Elizabeth for the current fee and inspection timing when you submit it.

The city's published detector rules give you a checklist to work from before you apply:

  • Smoke detectors on every level, including the basement and any finished attic, mounted at the center of the ceiling within ten feet of bedrooms.
  • A carbon monoxide detector on every floor near sleeping areas, with combination units allowed.
  • A UL listed 2-A:10-B:C fire extinguisher, fully charged and mounted within ten feet of the stove in every kitchen.
  • Hardwired systems must have power on and all units sounding together; battery units cannot replace a hardwired system.

Everything has to be mounted and working before the inspector arrives.

sections.h2: How do schools, transit and roads affect Elizabeth sales?
sections.html:
Elizabeth Public Schools is one of 31 former Abbott districts, and the state covers school construction costs there. It ran 36 schools and 28,712 students in 2018-19, Five new academies and a smaller Elizabeth High School came out of a split that began in 2009-10, when the old school had 5,300 students.

Transit is a real draw. NJ Transit stops at Elizabeth station and North Elizabeth on the Northeast Corridor and North Jersey Coast lines, with service to Newark Penn, Secaucus Junction and New York Penn. Buses run to the Port Authority terminal and to Newark. By road, the New Jersey Turnpike, Interstate 278, U.S. 1 and 9, and Routes 27, 28, 81 and 439 all cross the city. The Port Newark Elizabeth Marine Terminal and part of Newark Liberty airport sit within the city, and The Mills at Jersey Gardens anchors retail.

The Census says mean travel to work is 26.7 minutes.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Elizabeth buyers and sellers?
sections.html:
The population estimate rose 3.2 percent between April 2020 and July 2025, from a base of 137,306 to 141,675. Foreign-born residents make up 51.6 percent of the city, 77.1 percent of people over five speak a language other than English at home, and 67.4 percent identify as Hispanic or Latino. Persons per household average 2.95.

  • A bilingual listing, flyer and contract summary reaches more of those buyers.
  • Only 14.6 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree, while 74.2 percent have finished high school.
  • Retail sales were about $14,019 per resident in 2022.

Use these numbers to price realistically against the $449,300 median rather than against figures from richer Union County suburbs.

sections.h2: What is Elizabeth's history, and does it touch a sale?
sections.html:
English settlers founded Elizabethtown in 1664, and it served as New Jersey's first capital. The state legislature created the City of Elizabeth in 1855 and Union County was formed in 1857. The Singer Sewing Machine plant in Elizabethport once employed thousands, and the company left in 1982.

Elizabethport, the oldest neighborhood, grew around businesses serving ships, and Bayway grew up around the refinery on the Linden line. Whatever the age of your building, gather permit records and any boiler, roof or electrical paperwork before you list.

sections.h2: What should an Elizabeth seller gather before listing?
sections.html:
• The current block and lot numbers, confirmed with the Tax Assessor, since the city renumbered parcels starting January 1, 2023.
  • Proof of working, mounted detectors and extinguishers for every unit, ready for the smoke certificate attached to the resale application.
  • Permit records for any finished basement, converted attic or added unit.
  • Tenant names, lease terms and security deposit records if the building is occupied.
  • The deed, mortgage payoff figure and any lien letters.

Having all of this in one folder shortens the time between accepting an offer and sending a contract package to the buyer's attorney.

sections.h2: How are deeds and closing handled for an Elizabeth property?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded with the Union County Clerk, whose land records site is clerk.ucnj.org. A notice there says the city began assigning new lot and block numbers on January 1, 2023, and that the person preparing the deed must confirm the correct numbers with the Tax Assessor or the county tax board association before recording. The clerk is not responsible for numbers copied from an old document.

On the state side, the seller pays the realty transfer fee on the deed. Rates run per $500 of price and step up in bands, and sales over $1,000,000 add a graduated percent fee. A seller who is a New Jersey resident signs GIT/REP-3. Sellers who are nonresidents use GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 unless a listed assurance applies. Appeals of an assessment must reach the county board of taxation by April 1.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell my Elizabeth house?
faqs.a: Yes, Elizabeth runs a resale certificate program through an online application, and an occupied house needs its smoke detector certificate attached. Ask the city's Bureau of Zoning for the current fee and the inspection schedule.

faqs.q: What does Elizabeth require for detectors and extinguishers?
faqs.a: Smoke detectors on every level, carbon monoxide detectors on every floor near bedrooms, and a charged 2-A:10-B:C extinguisher within ten feet of the stove in each kitchen. All must be permanently mounted and working.

faqs.q: Which county office records an Elizabeth deed?
faqs.a: The Union County Clerk. Check the block and lot numbers first, because the city issued new ones starting January 1, 2023.

faqs.q: How many people live in Elizabeth?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 141,675 residents for July 1, 2025, up from 137,298 at the 2020 census.

faqs.q: When is the Elizabeth property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1, filed with the Union County Board of Taxation, or May 1 where the city has just completed a revaluation. Properties assessed above $1,000,000 may go to the State Tax Court instead.
